facts.value: Wikipedia says it was a major Abbasid-era public academy and intellectual center, also known as the Grand Library of Baghdad; dissolved 1258.
Origin is uncertain: founded either as a library for Harun al-Rashid (r. 786-809) or as a private collection of al-Mansur (r. 754-775); a Muslim Heritage article says Harun al-Rashid founded it.
facts.quote: founded either as a library for the collections of the fifth Abbasid caliph Harun al-Rashid

facts.value: Muslim Heritage Foundation: Abbasid caliph Harun al-Rashid founded the House of Wisdom in Baghdad during his reign (786-809).
facts.quote: Abbasid caliph Harun al-Rashid founded the House of Wisdom in Baghdad during his reign (786-809)

facts.value: Name Khizanat al-Hikma, Storehouse of Wisdom, appears in Ibn al-Nadim al-Fihrist (d. 995).
Sahl ibn Harun, a Persian poet and astrologer, was chief librarian of the Bayt al-Hikma (per Wikipedia).
facts.quote: Sahl ibn Harun, a Persian poet and astrologer, was the chief librarian of the Bayt al-Hikma

facts.value: Translation: Hunayn ibn Ishaq (809-873) was the most productive translator, producing 116 works for the Arabs (per Wikipedia).
facts.quote: was the most productive translator, producing 116 works for the Arabs

facts.value: Dimitri Gutas of Yale disputes the existence of the House of Wisdom as well as its form and function.
facts.quote: Yale University Arabist Dimitri Gutas disputes the existence of the House of Wisdom as well as its form and function

facts.value: Gutas notes that none of the Graeco-Arabic translations, including those of Hunayn ibn Ishaq, mention the House of Wisdom.
facts.quote: Gutas mentions that in all of the Graeco-Arabic translations none of them mention the House of Wisdom

facts.value: Wikipedia: considerably declined under al-Mutawakkil after flourishing under al-Mutasim and al-Wathiq.
facts.quote: but considerably declined under the reign of al-Mutawakkil

facts.value: Mongol destruction: Wikipedia says the House of Wisdom was destroyed with all other Baghdad libraries by Hulagu army; books thrown into the Tigris so that the river was said to run black.
facts.quote: the river was said to have run black

facts.value: Historian Michal Biran has shown that large libraries reopened for learning and teaching within two years of the siege (per the Siege of Baghdad article).
facts.quote: the historian Michal Biran has shown that large libraries reopened for learning and teaching within two years of the siege

events.label: Founded in the reign of Harun al-Rashid (786-809) per Muslim Heritage; origin disputed
events.quote: Abbasid caliph Harun al-Rashid founded the House of Wisdom in Baghdad during his reign (786-809)

events.label: Turned into a public academy and library under al-Mamun (r. 813-833), per Wikipedia
events.quote: it was turned into a public academy and a library

events.label: Said to be destroyed in the Mongol siege of Baghdad (13 February 1258 sack)
events.quote: It was destroyed in 1258 during the Mongol siege of Baghdad

events.label: Large libraries in Baghdad reopened within two years of the siege (Biran)
events.quote: large libraries reopened for learning and teaching within two years of the siege
